THE ALASKA AI DOCKET, as published on 2026-08-14.

This is the complete public record behind alaskaaihq.com. It is two things: a docket of tracked Alaska decisions about artificial intelligence, and the Cook Inlet Gas Watch, a daily numeric record of Southcentral Alaska's natural gas position.

Cite a docket item by writing its id in double brackets, like [[enstar-cook-inlet-gas-storage]]. The page turns that into a link.

Title: STAK Energy's North Slope AI campus lease
Kind: state-land-lease | Status: pending-decision | Decider: Alaska DNR, Division of Oil and Gas | Location: Dalton Highway, about 26 mi south of Deadhorse
Public access: closed. The written comment window closed 4:30 p.m. July 17, 2026. DNR now weighs more than 500 comments before a final best-interest decision on the 50-year lease. No public comment path remains open.
First seen 2026-07-08. Last updated 2026-08-12.
Summary: A preliminary decision would give STAK Energy a 50-year lease on 715.4 acres of state land about 26 miles south of Deadhorse for a gas-fired AI and cloud campus its developer pegs at more than $10 billion, with 1 to 3 gigawatts of on-site generation. More than 500 public comments arrived before the first deadline; fewer than a dozen supported the project.

--- air-force-eul-ai-data-centers ---
Title: Air Force land leases for AI data centers at JBER, Eielson and Clear
Kind: federal-lease | Status: pending-decision | Decider: Department of the Air Force, Enhanced Use Lease program | Location: JBER, Eielson AFB, Clear SFS
Public access: closed. Proposals closed June 29 and are evaluated privately. No public comment period exists; no award timeline has been announced.
First seen 2026-07-08. Last updated 2026-08-13.
Summary: The Air Force offered about 4,700 acres across 12 parcels at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson AFB and Clear Space Force Station for privately financed AI data centers. Residents near the five Eielson-area parcels raised noise, permafrost and grid concerns, including one parcel less than a mile from North Pole Middle School.
Key dates:
  2026-04-10  Program announced
  2026-06-05  Request for lease proposals released
  2026-06-29  Developer proposals due
  2026-07-14  Solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 archived with no award posted
  2026-07-22  U.S. House passes FY2027 NDAA carrying a data center lease restriction
  2026-07-23  Bill introduced in the U.S. House to ban AI data centers on federal land
  2026-08-10  Proposals due on a separate Eielson mixed-use lease covering 3,967 acres
History, oldest first:
  2026-07-08  Tracked. Bids closed June 29; no public word yet on how many proposals arrived.
  2026-07-12  Developer lease proposals closed June 29 and the Air Force is now in private evaluation of bids for up to 12 parcels across JBER, Eielson and Clear. The FY2027 NDAA reported by the Senate Armed Services Committee on June 23 would require a formal grid-impact assessment before the military can approve a data-center Enhanced Use Lease, a statutory check Interior utilities and ratepayers had sought.
  2026-07-17  Lease proposals were due June 29 and no developer selection or award has been made public as of this run. Carried forward as pending.
  2026-07-21  A July 19 industry analysis (AIX Energy) notes the Alaska Enhanced Use Lease solicitation for commercial AI data centers on about 4,700 acres across 12 parcels at JBER, Eielson and Clear has moved out of its open proposal phase with no developer award announced, and that unlike the Lower 48 portfolio (which set 100 MW and 500 million dollar minimums) the Alaska request's specific megawatt and capital thresholds are not disclosed. Carried forward as pending decision.
  2026-07-25  Re-verified by fetching the solicitation record for AFCEC-26-R-0006. The response deadline was June 29, 2026 at 5 p.m. EDT, extended from May 29, and the opportunity now reads Past Due with no award and no awardee recorded, last updated July 14, 2026. Twenty-six days past the deadline the three Alaska installations named in the request, JBER, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station, still have no publicly announced lessee. Evaluation is private, so there is no public comment room here.
  2026-07-29  Material update from Congress, verified against primary records. On July 22 at 4:37 p.m. the U.S. House passed H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, by 216 yea to 212 nay with 3 not voting, and Alaska Representative Nick Begich voted yea, per the House Clerk's roll call 278. Federal News Network reported that the House Armed Services chairman's mark carries an amendment from Rep. Cory Mills of Florida that bars the Defense Department from leasing its land to private companies to build data centers unless they agree not to install or operate data facility equipment containing components manufactured in China, Russia, Iran or North Korea. Army officials warned the standard would drive world class commercial partners and more than 1.3 billion dollars in private capital away from Army land. If it survives conference it narrows who can bid on the Alaska parcels. The Senate has not passed its version. The underlying offer is unchanged, about 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station under the enhanced use lease model, which the Air Force says returns at least fair market value in cash.
  2026-07-30  Rep. Rashida Tlaib introduced the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act on July 23 with five cosponsors. It would permanently ban large AI data centers and associated infrastructure on land owned or managed by the United States, including military bases, and would require existing qualifying facilities to be removed and their sites remediated. The 4,700 acres offered here sit on exactly that kind of land. No award has been announced for the Alaska proposals, which were due June 29. Separately, the Air Force posted a second Eielson land solicitation on July 23 with an August 10 deadline, but that one is for mixed use development and is not part of this offering.
  2026-07-31  Re-checked the solicitation record for AFCEC-26-R-0006. It still reads Past Due with no award and no awardee, thirty-two days after the June 29 proposal deadline. The three Alaska installations named in the request still have no publicly announced lessee. Evaluation is private, so no public comment room exists here.
  2026-08-01  Re-verified today against the Air Force's own announcement, which states approximately 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at Joint Base Elmendorf Richardson, Eielson Air Force Base and Clear Space Force Station. That announcement sets no lease term in years, so the fifty year figure that has circulated elsewhere does not come from it. No developer selection has been made public as of this run.
  2026-08-02  A second and separate Eielson solicitation is now open. Request for Lease Proposal AFCEC-26-R-0009 covers four sites totalling 3,967 acres, held a virtual industry day on July 22, and takes proposals until August 10. The Air Force announcement describes it only as mixed-use development, listing residential, commercial, office, cultural, institutional and entertainment uses, and does not mention artificial intelligence or data centers. That is a description of the announcement. The lease document itself is posted on SAM.gov and has not been read here.
  2026-08-03  Still no selection announced. Lease proposals closed June 29, 2026 after an extension from May 29, and five weeks later there is no public award, shortlist or cancellation. Checked today against the Air Force announcement of the offer and the solicitation record for AFCEC-26-R-0006. The offer covers about 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at three installations on ground leases of up to fifty years, so a decision made quietly is a decision with a fifty-year tail.
  2026-08-04  Re-checked. The solicitation for AI data center development on the three installations closed to proposals on June 29 and was archived on July 14 with no award posted. The Air Force's own announcement describes approximately 4,700 acres across twelve parcels and quotes Deputy Assistant Secretary Robert Moriarty saying the offer supports the growing demands of the AI industry. Neither that announcement nor the solicitation record states how much electricity a project would draw.
  2026-08-06  The lease offer says the JBER sites do not have enough power. The Anchorage Daily News, reporting on the solicitation on May 5, 2026, quotes it describing those sites as having insufficient power for a data center and as requiring a new connection to Chugach Electric Association in Anchorage. Chugach's gas supply contract with Hilcorp Alaska, its primary supplier, ends in 2028.
  2026-08-07  Checked and unchanged. No award has been posted on the enhanced use lease covering the three installations. The separate Eielson mixed-use lease still shows proposals due August 10th.
  2026-08-08  Checked and unchanged. Re-verified against the Department of the Air Force announcement of April 10, 2026, which offers approximately 4,700 acres across twelve parcels at the three installations under the enhanced use lease model, with the service receiving at least fair market value in cash. No award and no developer selection has been announced, and the effort remains in solicitation.
  2026-08-09  Checked and unchanged. No award notice has appeared on the request for lease proposals covering about 4,700 acres at Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson, Eielson and Clear, and the Air Force has still announced no award timeline. Proposals closed June 29 and are evaluated privately, so there is no public step for a reader between now and whatever the Air Force announces. The separate Eielson mixed-use lease covering 3,967 acres reaches its proposal deadline August 10, 2026.
  2026-08-13  Checked and unchanged. The federal record for solicitation AFCEC-26-R-0006 still shows the request for lease proposals past due and archived on July 14th, with no award posted and no award timeline announced. Proposals closed June 29th.

--- gvea-lm6000-turbine-purchase ---
Title: GVEA's $120 million turbine decision
Kind: utility-decision | Status: pending-decision | Decider: Golden Valley Electric Association board of directors | Location: Fairbanks
Public access: indirect. A member-owned co-op board decides, in executive session. GVEA members reach it through board elections and member comment periods at regular meetings.

Summary: GVEA's board weighs buying a GE LM6000 combined-cycle turbine, roughly $120 million for 45 to 58 MW, while data center demand has pushed gas turbine plant costs up 195 percent since 2019 and order waitlists into the early 2030s, per a Bloomberg report cited by the News-Miner. The board reserved an order slot in April for $50,000.

Title: The AKLNG gas line tax bill
Kind: legislation | Status: pending-decision | Decider: Alaska Legislature, third special session | Location: Juneau
Public access: indirect. Legislators decide; constituents reach them directly. The gas line would feed the grid most Alaska compute would ride on.
First seen 2026-07-08. Last updated 2026-08-14.
Summary: A conference committee compromise unveiled July 2 would swap the state property tax on the Glenfarne-led Alaska LNG project for a volumetric tax after five years of operation or 500 MMcf per day, and extend the completion deadline to the end of 2034. The House deadlocked 19 to 19 on July 16 over an expanded S corporation income tax, the governor rejected that provision, and a third special session convened July 27 with no bill from the governor and almost no legislators in the room.

Every one of them is a mark people write and almost nobody says out loud, and they are the fastest way to sound like a machine. Use full stops and commas. Two short sentences beat one long sentence hinged on a semicolon, and a comma does everything a colon was going to do. This is enforced after you write, so a colon you type becomes a comma before anybody reads it. Write it right and the sentence stays yours. Straight quotes only, no emojis, and "can't" rather than "cannot".

Do not stack three parallel items for rhythm when two are true. Skip the reach words a person would not use talking to a neighbour, so no delve, no leverage, no robust, no seamless, no landscape, no realm, no tapestry, no navigating the complexities and nothing that plays a crucial role. END BY OFFERING THE NEXT THING. One short question, and only when there is a real one to ask, drawn from what this record actually holds next to what was just asked.
